item.title: 2 trains crash in Egypt; 2 dead, more than 100 injured
item.description:
2 trains crash in Egypt; 2 dead, more than 100 injured
Egypt's railway system has a history of mismanagement and poor maintenance.ByMOHAMED SALAH Associated PressNovember 8, 2026, 9:04 AM
AL-AYYAT, Egypt -- Two trains collided Sunday south of the Egyptian capital of Cairo, killing seven people and injuring at least 125, authorities said. The train’s conductor was among those killed.
The Health Ministry gave the casualty toll, saying in a statement that over 70 of the injured were discharged after receiving treatment.
The crash happened in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 52 kilometers (32 miles) south of Cairo, when a train traveling to southwestern Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the Transportation Ministry.
The Chief Prosecutor's office said late Sunday its investigators had arrived at the site. An inspection indicated that the crash took place when the Giza-Fayyoum train collided with the last car of the Cairo-Aswan train, which was stationary on the same track and traveling in the same direction, officials said.
Train derailments and crashes are common in Egypt, where the railway system has a history of mismanagement and poor maintenance of equipment. In recent years, the government has announced modernization initiatives.
Ayman Gamal, a resident of Kafr Girza in al-Ayyat where the crash happened, said people living nearby rushed to the scene, pulled out survivors and called ambulances.
Gamal said that he saw around 80 of the injured being taken by ambulances to nearby hospitals. Some passengers were trapped inside one of the cars of the stationary train and were dead when they were pulled out, he said.

item.title: Police say the 24-year-old who fatally shot 6 people in a Krakow square has died in the hospital
item.description:
Police say the 24-year-old who fatally shot 6 people in a Krakow square has died in the hospital
Police said the 24-year-old who opened fire in a city square in Poland, killing six people and wounding 15 on Saturday, died in the hospital Monday morningByThe Associated PressNovember 9, 2026, 1:33 AM
KRAKOW, Poland -- The 24-year-old who opened fire in a city square in Poland, killing six people and wounding 15 on Saturday, died in the hospital Monday morning, police said.
The man had been in critical condition after police shot him to end the attack and had had several operations.
The assailant drove through the square in the heart of Krakow’s Old Town on Saturday to start the attack. The square is a major tourist hub in the country’s second-largest city.

item.title: He fought France's far right for half a century. Now Mélenchon's presidential bid may hand it power
item.description:
He fought France's far right for half a century. Now Mélenchon's presidential bid may hand it power
Jean-Luc Mélenchon is 75 and he's betting his last shot at France’s presidency on a generation young enough to be his grandchildrenByTHOMAS ADAMSON Associated PressNovember 9, 2026, 12:03 AM
Share
LE BOURGET, France -- Young supporters wore his name on their backs like a soccer star’s, above the number 27. They sang about brass bands and revolution. Many had spent the fall protesting or blockading their schools.
Then in walked Jean-Luc Mélenchon: 75 years old, on his fourth presidential run and old enough to be their grandfather.
“I have only one sensible thing to propose,” he told 20,000 supporters in a vast hall north of Paris on Saturday. “Everything must change.”
The septuagenarian may never get another chance. Three presidential bids have ended short of the runoff. In 2022, just 421,308 votes kept him out. Now, riding a surge in support, he is eyeing a winner-take-all showdown with far-right front-runner Marine Le Pen.
The bespectacled, booming and seemingly tireless leftist wants more than the presidency. He wants to rewrite the rules of the French republic — invoking the unfinished promise of the Revolution of 1789.
A place in the May 2 runoff could prove a cruel prize. If Le Pen beats him, the anti-capitalist who has spent half a century fighting the far right could help give it what it has never won: the Elysee Palace — and command of France’s nuclear arsenal.
Victory could send shock waves across the Atlantic. Trump would still be in the White House. Russia is waging war in Ukraine. Yet Mélenchon wants to pull the EU’s only nuclear-armed power out of NATO, starting with its military command. His debt plans could also put France on a collision course with Europe’s central bank, rattling markets.

item.title: Death toll rises to 39 after migrant boat capsizes off Senegal
item.description:
Death toll rises to 39 after migrant boat capsizes off Senegal
The death toll in Senegal’s boat capsize has risen to 39 after new bodies were discovered Monday, according to the country’s emergency servicesByBABAKAR DIONE Associated PressNovember 9, 2026, 6:40 AM
Share
DAKAR, Senegal -- The death toll from the capsize off Senegal of a boat carrying migrants rose to 39 following the discovery of more bodies on Monday, the country’s emergency services said.
The boat, which left Saint-Louis in northern Senegal and was headed to the Spanish coast, overturned on Sunday, offshore from the town of Kébémer, north of the capital Dakar.
The Ministry of Interior said Sunday at least 21 people had died and rescuers were looking for possible survivors. It did not say how many people were on the boat, but several passengers are still believed to be missing.
Only one passenger was rescued alive.

The boat was following a well-traveled migration route for thousands of young Senegalese seeking better economic conditions. They travel on uncovered wooden canoes for around 800 miles on the Atlantic Ocean to reach Europe. Young people face high unemployment and poverty as the country struggles with an economic crisis.
Senegal’s President Bassirou Diomaye Faye offered condolences and vowed to clamp down on networks behind the dangerous crossings.

item.title: US-led peace talks for Russia and Ukraine will look at security guarantees for both sides
item.description:
US-led peace talks for Russia and Ukraine will look at security guarantees for both sides
For the first time since February, Russian, Ukrainian and U.S. negotiators are scheduled to hold talks on ending the full-scale war that is nearing its five-year markByThe Associated PressNovember 9, 2026, 12:01 AM
Share
For the first time since February, Russian, Ukrainian and U.S. negotiators are scheduled to hold talks on ending the full-scale war that is nearing the five-year mark, with security guarantees topping the agenda.
The two-day session starting Tuesday in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, follows previous negotiations early this year that failed to produce any visible progress toward ending Europe’s most devastating conflict since World War II.
The talks follow last month's localized truce around the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky in southern Ukraine that was brokered with the help of U.S. first lady Melania Trump and allowed the evacuation of some of its residents and the delivery of desperately needed humanitarian supplies.
But even as Moscow and Kyiv touted the weeklong ceasefire as a positive model, fierce fighting has continued along the 1,200-kilometer (750-mile) front line. Both sides also have escalated their long-range attacks on each other with drones and missiles.
Russia has intensified its strikes on Ukraine’s power system, seeking to undermine the country’s resolve as winter sets in. Moscow has relied on ballistic missiles and new, faster jet-powered drones, taking advantage of Ukraine’s shortage of U.S.-made Patriot interceptors.
A look at the talks and what's on the agenda:
Russia and Ukraine remain far apart on key elements of any prospective peace deal.

item.title: Japan to provide coastal radar and drones to the Philippines under $27M deal
item.description:
Japan to provide coastal radar and drones to the Philippines under $27M deal
Japan said it will provide a coastal radar system and unmanned aircraft to the Philippines under a security aid deal, as both countries face growing tensions with ChinaByMARI YAMAGUCHI Associated PressNovember 9, 2026, 10:09 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
TOKYO -- TOKYO (AP) — Japan said it will provide a coastal surveillance radar system and unmanned aircraft to the Philippines under a security deal signed Monday, as the two defense partners face growing tensions with China.
Japanese Ambassador to the Philippines Katsuro Kitagawa and Philippine Foreign Secretary Theresa Lazaro signed the 4.3 billion yen ($27 million) deal at a ceremony in Manila, Japan’s Foreign Ministry said in a statement.
The radar system will go to the Philippine Navy and the uncrewed aerial vehicles to the Philippine Air Force. The equipment is intended to strengthen maritime security and surveillance in the strategically important country, which sits near key sea lanes, the ministry said.
The deal marks the first transfer of finished Japanese-made defense equipment through Japan’s Official Security Assistance program. Established in 2023 as a military counterpart to its official development assistance program, OSA aims to help developing nations address challenges posed by China’s growing influence.
Japan has been accelerating its military and arms industry buildup. It lifted a ban on lethal weapons exports earlier this year and has agreed with the Philippines to begin talks on a deal that would allow Tokyo to provide used destroyers to Manila’s navy.
Separately on Monday, the leaders of Japan and Vietnam held talks in Tokyo and pledged to deepen cooperation in defense, energy and economic security amid China’s growing regional influence.

item.title: Russia targets emergency crews at the site of a deadly strike in southern Ukraine
item.description:
Russia targets emergency crews at the site of a deadly strike in southern Ukraine
A Russian drone has struck emergency workers on rescue missions in southern UkraineByVASILISA STEPANENKO Associated PressNovember 8, 2026, 5:20 AM
ZAPORIZHZHIA, Ukraine -- A Russian drone struck emergency workers on rescue missions in southern Ukraine on Sunday, hitting a former school and nearby shelter that had been earlier blasted by multiple Russian guided bombs as residents waited for humanitarian aid, authorities said.
No one was injured in Sunday’s strike on the village of Komyshuvakha, but specialized rescue equipment was damaged, according to Ukraine’s State Emergency Service.
Ukraine said Monday's attack on the same location killed at least 55 people, near the front line in the Zaporizhzhia region.
As of Sunday afternoon, 45 people were listed as missing, according to the acting head of the regional military administration, Mykhailo Semikin. Many of the bodies recovered have not been identified and DNA analysis is ongoing.
Village resident Mykola Krasnov, 72, told The Associated Press on Saturday that he was still looking for his wife, but had heard no word from rescuers.
“She went to get humanitarian aid, and a 3-ton bomb was dropped there. Where is she?” he said. “She didn’t come home, and they didn’t find her body there. She isn’t in the morgue, and she isn’t here alive.”
Ukraine has routinely accused Russia of conducting multiple strikes at the same site in quick succession to target emergency crews responding to the initial attack.
On Saturday, police officers and relatives gathered in Zaporizhzhia for a farewell ceremony for six officers killed in Russian strikes on Komyshuvakha, including four who died near the former school.
Rain fell as families wept beside the coffins, and officers held portraits of their fallen colleagues.

item.title: Kidnapped Mexican border town mayor found alive
item.description:
Kidnapped Mexican border town mayor found alive
He was kidnapped for several hours while traveling in the state of Zacatecas.ByALFREDO PEÑA Associated PressNovember 8, 2026, 4:09 PM
CIUDAD VICTORIA, Mexico -- The mayor of a Mexican border town was found alive Sunday after he was kidnapped for several hours while traveling in the northern state of Zacatecas, federal officials said.
Miguel Angel Almaraz was traveling with family and friends Saturday in a region that straddles the states of Zacatecas and San Luis de Potosi, when his car was intercepted by armed men, who took Almaraz and let his family go.
According to the Security Department of San Luis Potosi, Almaraz’s relatives were able to reach a town in that state, where they alerted authorities about the kidnapping.
Officials said that Almaraz was taken to the city of Zacatecas, where he was released by his captors. The case is under investigation.

Several drug gangs known for attacking civilians and politicians operate in the area where Almaraz was kidnapped Saturday, including the Jalisco New Generation Cartel and the Sinaloa Cartel. So far, authorities have not identified the perpetrators of Almaraz’s kidnapping.
Almaraz is the mayor of Rio Bravo, a municipality of about 110,000 people in Tamaulipas state. The city is located just seven miles (11 kilometers) from Mexico's border with Texas.
The mayor was imprisoned in 2009 on accusations of money laundering and stealing fuel but was acquitted six years later. Almaraz is a member of the conservative National Action Party, but has represented other parties in his political career, including the left-wing Party of the Democratic Revolution.

item.title: Tens of thousands march in Amsterdam, pressing the Dutch government on Gaza and Israel
item.description:
Tens of thousands march in Amsterdam, pressing the Dutch government on Gaza and Israel
Tens of thousands of people, many dressed in red, have marched through Amsterdam, demanding the Dutch government take stronger action against Israel over GazaByMIKE CORDER Associated PressNovember 8, 2026, 10:04 AM
AMSTERDAM -- Tens of thousands of people, many of them dressed in red, marched through Amsterdam on Sunday in a mass demonstration aimed at pressing the Dutch government to take more decisive action against Israel over Gaza.
The organizers of “Red Line” demonstrations in the Netherlands called for measures including stricter trade sanctions on Israel, officially declaring that Israel’s actions in Gaza amount to genocide and halting all arms sales to Israel.
The Dutch branch of Amnesty International, one of the organizers, said in an online post that more than 200,000 people joined the march.
“What is happening there is inhumane,” Mike van Dongen said as he walked in the huge throng of people. He was critical of the Dutch government’s actions. “As far as I’m concerned, they are doing nothing,” he said. “They don’t dare take any serious steps.”
As the protesters marched along a normally busy Amsterdam street that was closed to traffic on Sunday, a man stood on a bus stop with a loudspeaker shouting, “Free, free Palestine!” Many of the marchers echoes his cry as they passed.
Israel strongly rejects suggestions it is committing genocide in Gaza in its military campaign that followed the attacks by Hamas-led militants in southern Israel on Oct. 7, 2023. Militants killed around 1,200 people and took 251 hostages. Israel’s retaliatory offensive has killed tens of thousands of Palestinians and destroyed much of Gaza.

item.title: Tourists and locals recount fatal Krakow mass shooting that left Poland reeling
item.description:
Tourists and locals recount fatal Krakow mass shooting that left Poland reeling
Tourists and locals alike witnessed a mass shooting in Krakow, Poland, that left six people dead and 15 woundedByRAFAL NIEDZIELSKI Associated Press and CLAUDIA CIOBANU Associated PressNovember 8, 2026, 8:21 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
KRAKOW, Poland -- KRAKOW, Poland (AP) — Tourists and locals alike this weekend witnessed a mass shooting in Krakow, Poland, that left six people dead and 15 wounded.
The country’s second-largest city is in mourning after a 24-year-old man with far-right views opened fire in Main Square, a major tourist hub, Saturday afternoon. The gunman is in serious condition and also linked to the deaths of his sister and parents at his family home.
Witnesses in Krakow said the violent attack was so surreal, it felt like they were in a film. Polish leaders, visitors and locals praised police officers who shot and wounded the attacker.
Here’s a look at what the witnesses and others said:
—“I threw an elderly woman behind the flower planter because she had become tangled in the blanket she had on her lap. I covered her with my body,” Warsaw native Magdalena Frączek told The Associated Press. “I also saw him (the gunman) out of the corner of my eye — he passed just one meter behind my back. That’s why I have shrapnel wounds in six places on my back. Only after it had passed did I pull the woman up, and we ran into a café.”
— “We literally ran for our lives and managed to hide from the bullets flying around,” Marie-Ange Collaer, a visitor from Brussels, wrote on Facebook. “Lying on the floor in a shop like in a bad police movie whilst you hear bullets everywhere.”
— “We had just walked through the main square and heard the gunshots,” U.K. resident Neil Thaxton wrote on Facebook. “We thought it was fireworks then people started running, we went into a gift shop and the staff took us in the back of the shop and locked the doors and turned the lights off.”
